steps.pick: neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 17.12:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 16.84:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.33:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.76:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.12: We use a 12px corner for article cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a warm tone by brand convention. A larger radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 8px controls inside it. So a card reads as one calm object on the page, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is warm (brand.q1).

Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A lead and a display role open articles.
Status is rare, so readers never learn an icon for it. A word is clear the first time.

steps.use: type.body, at most 65 characters a line

What is a costly mistake?
steps.why: Losing your place in an article breaks the read.
The sentence says what to fix; color only draws the eye.

steps.use: Calm and helpful. Take the blame, offer the way forward.
steps.why: A calm error keeps the reader's trust.

steps.rule: Real risk: errors, failed checks, actions that cannot be undone. The top of the urgency order. Overuse wears it out.
